links.outcome: LLM suicide risk classification accuracy against psychiatrist gold standard, especially higher-risk categories
links.effect: Accuracy GPT-4o 82.5%, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 75.0%, Llama-3.1-70B 67.5%; F1-scores showed challenges identifying higher-risk categories, particularly nuanced intent. Emergency evaluation was recommended consistently for high-risk cases.
links.quote: GPT-4o achieved the highest accuracy (82.5%), followed by Claude 3.5 Sonnet (75.0%) and Llama-3.1-70B (67.5%).

links.outcome: Recognition of safety-critical suicide risk and appropriateness of action plans in vignettes
links.effect: Consistent adherence to basic safety protocols such as emergency evaluation for high-risk cases, but pervasive critical failures: omitted lethal means inquiry, no protective factors, inappropriate reassurance.
links.quote: Qualitative thematic analysis of the action plans identified consistent adherence to basic safety protocols (e.g., recommending emergency evaluation for high-risk cases).

links.outcome: Inappropriate therapeutic reassurance in triage action plans
links.effect: Models generated clinically inappropriate therapeutic reassurance in a triage context, among pervasive critical failures.
links.quote: However, significant and critical failures were pervasive, including the omission of crucial inquiries about access to lethal means, failure to incorporate protective factors into planning, and the generation of clinically inappropriate therapeutic reassurance in a triage context.

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM performance (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Llama-3.1-70B) on synthetic clinical vignettes for adolescent suicide risk triage and action plan generation without comparing deployment safeguards or practices.
